title: Report Timetable to Adjusters and Employers (Workers' Compensation Referral)
content:
# Report timetable — Workers' Compensation Referral

Reports on a Workers' Compensation Referral go to the adjuster or, for an employer direct program, to the employer. The timetable fixes, per program, when the initial evaluation report (or the FCE report) is due, the longest gap allowed between progress reports, whether a work status update follows each program day, when the discharge report is due, how quickly a missed visit is reported, and whether reports are copied to the nurse case manager assigned on the claim.

| Program | Initial (or FCE) report due (business days) | Progress report interval (calendar days) | Work status update after every program day | Discharge report due (calendar days) | Missed visit reported within (business days) | Copy to nurse case manager |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Employer Direct Early Intervention | 1 | 7 | No | 3 | 1 | No |
| Workers' Comp Outpatient Therapy | 2 | 30 | No | 7 | 1 | Yes |
| Workers' Comp Post-Surgical Therapy | 2 | 30 | No | 7 | 1 | Yes |
| Work Conditioning Program | 2 | 14 | Yes | 5 | 1 | Yes |
| Work Hardening Program | 2 | 7 | Yes | 5 | 1 | Yes |
| Functional Capacity Evaluation | 5 | 0 | No | 0 | 1 | Yes |

## Definitions

- **Initial report due** — the business days after the initial evaluation (or the FCE) within which its report is sent.
- **Progress report interval** — the most calendar days allowed between progress reports to the adjuster or employer; 0 where only a final report is sent.
- **Work status update after every program day** — whether a work status update is sent after every program day.
- **Discharge report due** — the calendar days after discharge within which the discharge report is sent; 0 where the final report is the FCE report.
- **Missed visit reported within** — the business days after a missed visit within which it is reported to the adjuster or employer.
- **Copy to nurse case manager** — whether every report is copied to the nurse case manager assigned on the claim.

## Comparisons

- Progress reports run every 7 days in Employer Direct Early Intervention and Work Hardening Program, every 14 days in Work Conditioning Program and every 30 days in the two therapy programs; Functional Capacity Evaluation shows 0 because only its final report is sent.
- The initial report is due in 1 business day for Employer Direct Early Intervention, 2 for the four treatment programs, and 5 for the Functional Capacity Evaluation report.
- The discharge report is due in 3 calendar days (Employer Direct Early Intervention), 7 (the two therapy programs) or 5 (Work Conditioning and Work Hardening); Functional Capacity Evaluation shows 0.
- Every program reports a missed visit within 1 business day.
- Only Work Conditioning and Work Hardening send a work status update after every program day; every program except Employer Direct Early Intervention copies the nurse case manager.
